My land is only 1.2 mu — just one small plot behind the house. I am 72 now, and I work it alone since my household is just me. I have done this wheat-maize rotation for 40 years, same as everyone in our village.

For the winter wheat, I will sow in early October after the maize comes off. I use improved seed — I buy it from the agricultural supply shop in town, the same variety my neighbor Old Wang used last year because he got over 450 kg. Before sowing I spread compound fertilizer as base, about one bag (50 kg) of 15-15-15 for my plot, which works out to around 42 kg total, plus some urea. In spring when the wheat turns green I topdress urea again, maybe 15 kg on the whole plot. For my 1.2 mu that means nitrogen around 18 kg per mu, phosphorus 6, potassium 6. I would rather put a little extra than watch the wheat turn yellow — fertilizer money is small compared to losing the harvest.

I irrigate the wheat from my well — once before winter to help it survive the cold, once at returning-green in March, once at jointing, and once at grain filling if the spring is dry. That is 3 to 4 times. I spray once for aphids and powdery mildew around April, sometimes twice if the weather is wet. I plough with the village tractor service before sowing — rotary tillage, it costs less than deep ploughing and my soil is not too hard.

For summer maize I sow right after the wheat harvest in mid-June, no tillage, just seed into the stubble — this saves time and the ground stays moist. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Xianyu type, whatever the shop has fresh. I put one bag of compound fertilizer as base and topdress urea at the big trumpet stage. Maize needs more nitrogen than wheat — about 20 kg per mu. Since I fertilized well for wheat, I use less phosphorus and potassium on the maize. I irrigate once or twice depending on summer rain — usually our rainy season covers most of the need. I spray once for corn borer.

My yields have been steady — wheat around 450 kg per mu, maize around 550 kg per mu. I do not chase record yields at my age. Steady is good.
